evidence.paraphrase: The society has eliminated prisons, poverty, and war.
evidence.quote:
There were no prisons, no slums, no insane asylums, no cripples, no
poverty, no wars.

evidence.paraphrase: Disease and aging have been cured.
evidence.quote: All diseases were conquered. So was old age.

evidence.paraphrase: The national population is held fixed at forty million.
evidence.quote:
The population of the United States was stabilized at forty-million
souls.

evidence.paraphrase: Because aging is cured, death only comes to those who volunteer for it.
evidence.quote: Death, barring accidents, was an adventure for volunteers.

evidence.paraphrase: The average lifespan is now around 129, making a 56-year-old young.
evidence.quote:
Wehling was fifty-six, a mere stripling in a population whose average
age was one hundred and twenty-nine.

evidence.paraphrase: Law requires a volunteer death for each newborn to be allowed to live.
evidence.quote:
The law said that no newborn child could survive unless the parents of
the child could find someone who would volunteer to die.

evidence.paraphrase: A government agency operates gas chambers accessible by phone number.
evidence.quote:
"To be or not to be" was the telephone number of the municipal gas
chambers of the Federal Bureau of Termination.

evidence.paraphrase: A cure for aging was discovered at a certain point.
evidence.quote:
Aging had
touched him that much before the cure for aging was found.

evidence.paraphrase: Hitz explains that population control prevents catastrophic overcrowding.
evidence.quote:
Without population
control, human beings would now be packed on this surface of this old
planet like drupelets on a blackberry!

evidence.paraphrase: Hitz describes runaway population growth that justified the new controls.
evidence.quote:
Would you like to go back to the good old days, when the population of
the Earth was twenty billion--about to become forty billion, then eighty
billion, then one hundred and sixty billion?

evidence.paraphrase: Prior overpopulation led to shortages of water and food until scientists intervened.
evidence.quote:
In the year 2000," said Dr. Hitz, "before scientists stepped in and
laid down the law, there wasn't even enough drinking water to go around,
and nothing to eat but sea-weed

evidence.paraphrase: Hitz contrasts the past hellish crowded world with the present peaceful plenty.
evidence.quote:
Two centuries ago, when I was a young man,
it was a hell that nobody thought could last another twenty years. Now
centuries of peace and plenty stretch before us as far as the
imagination cares to travel.

evidence.paraphrase: Wehling expresses that he wants all three of his newborn children.
evidence.quote: "I want those kids," said Wehling quietly. "I want all three of them."

evidence.paraphrase: Wehling murders Dr. Hitz to make room for a child.
evidence.quote:
Wehling shot Dr. Hitz dead. "There's room for one--a great big one," he
said.

evidence.paraphrase: Wehling kills himself and two others so all three children can live.
evidence.quote: And then he shot himself, making room for all three of his children.

evidence.paraphrase: The painter is so affected he decides to stop painting.
evidence.quote:
He knew that he would never paint again. He let his paintbrush fall to
the dropcloths below.

evidence.paraphrase: The painter decides he is done with living.
evidence.quote:
And then he decided he had had about enough of
life in the Happy Garden of Life, too

evidence.paraphrase: The painter reflects on the fundamental problem of unlimited life on a finite planet.
evidence.quote:
The painter pondered the mournful puzzle of life demanding to be born
and, once born, demanding to be fruitful ... to multiply and to live as
long as possible--to do all that on a very small planet that would have
to last forever.

evidence.paraphrase: The painter concludes alternatives to termination are worse: war, plague, starvation.
evidence.quote:
All the answers that the painter could think of were grim. Even grimmer,
surely, than a Catbox, a Happy Hooligan, an Easy Go. He thought of war.
He thought of plague. He thought of starvation.

evidence.paraphrase: X-ray imaging revealed triplets before birth.
evidence.quote: X-rays had revealed that his wife was going to have triplets.

evidence.paraphrase: Gas-chamber hostesses reportedly grow mustaches after years of the work.
evidence.quote:
A curious thing about gas-chamber hostesses was that, no matter how lovely
and feminine they were when recruited, they all sprouted mustaches
within five years or so.
